problems.field: ai_available_when_produced (and the question code that rests on it)
problems.form_value: yes for all five outcomes; question with_ai
problems.source_says: The AI-generated images appear only in the PowerPoint slides of the teacher-instruction segment of Stage 3. Painting practice is a second segment of the same stage. No sentence says the slides stayed in view, or that the images were otherwise available, while students painted. The paper states neither yes nor no, so 'yes' is an inference from the shared 40-minute stage, and form-spec rule 1 says not to infer. The form admits the gap in S1-O1's measure_detail and in the reconciliation, but it codes 'yes' without qualification for all five outcomes and leaves the gap out of open_questions. with_ai is still the closest question code: there is no later unassisted session, and after_ai describes work after a period of AI use. Fix: keep with_ai and add an open question that the paper does not say whether the AI images were available during painting.
problems.quote: This stage consists of two components: teacher instruction and student painting practice.
problems.locator: p. 6, Stage 3; p. 4, Methods, Participants ('structured exposure to AI-generated images'); form-spec rule 1; codebook section 1

problems.source_says: Technical Skill rates how well the student applied the techniques taught in class. Composition and Design rates how space, balance, and harmony are used. Neither item asks about usefulness, feasibility, or appropriateness, and the paper groups the whole rubric under RQ4, 'painting skills'. The only support is the phrase 'quality of a single output' in codebook section 6. The c059 reconciliation read that phrase narrowly and coded a writing-proficiency composite 'other' because it was 'not judged for creativity, novelty, or the usefulness of ideas'. The same reasoning gives 'other' for these two craft ratings. Adherence to Theme (S1-O3) is the rubric's appropriateness item and fits usefulness. The form already flags this choice in open_questions. No pooled with_ai record changes, because S1-O1 is the primary record under either code.
problems.quote: (1) Technical Skill: How effectively did the student apply the techniques taught in class?
problems.locator: p. 6, Stage 4, rubric items (1) and (3); p. 2, Introduction, RQ4; codebook section 6, Construct; forms/c059.json, reconciliation of S1-O1 construct

problems.field: notes (list of paper inconsistencies) and ai_tool.how_used
problems.form_value: how_used: 'Students did not operate the AI.' The notes list five inconsistencies in the paper but not this one.
problems.source_says: Two Discussion passages say students took part in generating images and could experiment with GAI before refining their work by hand. The procedure says the opposite: both groups painted with identical traditional tools (p. 6), and students could not use the tool themselves because a research assistant made the images (p. 12). The procedure text supports the form's codes, so no code changes. The conflict bears directly on AI availability while painting, and it belongs in notes beside the other inconsistencies. Low severity.
problems.quote: By involving students in the image generation process through AI, they become more engaged in the lesson and are likely to remain focused on the task.
problems.locator: p. 9, Discussion, 'Firstly' paragraph; p. 11, Discussion, 'Fourthly' paragraph ('GAI enables rapid prototyping allowing students to experiment freely with diverse techniques'); contrast p. 6, Stage 3, and p. 12, fourth limitation

confirmed: All five outcomes are scores that three teachers gave each student's Task 2 painting on a 1 to 5 rubric. None is a self-report. The Discussion's 'satisfaction' wording conflicts, but the Methods and Results name the teachers as raters and report their agreement (p. 6, Stage 4; p. 8, Results, Visual art work; p. 9, ICC 0.847; p. 11, Table 9).

measure expert_raters fits codebook section 6, which includes instructors. The raters are two art teachers (24 and 4 years of teaching) and one math teacher (3 years). Rater Z is the experiment's instructor (p. 8, Results, Visual art work; p. 10, Table 8).

Every number in the five 'reported' fields matches Table 9 on the page image, including n = 39 per arm and the row label 'Creativity and Originalit'. The Results text repeats the Technical Skill numbers (p. 11, Table 9; pp. 8-9, Results, Visual art work).

The printed t values reproduce from the printed means and SDs with n = 39 per arm: 2.551, 2.547, 2.725, 3.515, and 3.499 against printed 2.554, 2.550, 2.725, 3.515, and 3.502. The printed p values match one-sided tests (two-sided: 0.013, 0.013, 0.008, 0.0007, 0.0008), as the form's open_questions says (p. 11, Table 9).

unit participant matches the paper's analysis: independent-samples t-tests with n = 39 per arm and one painting per student ('create and design a distinct and characteristic anthropomorphic cartoon character'). All ten arm means are multiples of 1/117 (for example 4.581 = 536/117), which fits each student's score being the mean of three raters' integer scores (p. 6, Stage 3; p. 8, Results; p. 11, Table 9).
timing immediate: students painted in the same Stage 3 lesson of about 40 minutes in which the teacher showed the examples (p. 6, Stage 3).

comparison_type ai_vs_active: the control lesson used classical artworks of iconic cartoon characters, which are human-made examples (p. 6, Stage 3; p. 8, Fig. 4). direction treatment_higher holds on all five criteria (p. 11, Table 9).

Students did not operate the AI in the procedure: a research assistant generated the images, and both groups painted with sketching pencils, watercolor paints, and art paper (p. 6, Stage 3; p. 12, fourth limitation).

S1-O1 overall_creativity is supported by the item label 'Creativity and Originality: How unique and imaginative is the artwork?'. A novelty reading is also defensible, and S1-O1 is the primary with_ai record under either code (p. 6, Stage 4 rubric; codebook section 8).
S1-O3 usefulness fits: 'Did the student follow the assignment guidelines or theme?' rates appropriateness to the brief. S1-O5 other fits a rating of effort and progress (p. 6, Stage 4 rubric).

No outcome that bears on the three questions is missing. The paper announces Task 1 painting ratings, a painting ANCOVA, a composite score, and treatment-group interviews, but prints no results for any of them (only the composite's ICC). Engagement, self-efficacy, and cognitive load are questionnaires (p. 5, Fig. 2; p. 6, Data analysis; p. 9; pp. 8-9, Tables 3-7).
No diversity outcome and no later unassisted session exist, so no outcome is across_people or after_ai. The paper mentions homogenization only as a risk reported in other studies (p. 11, Discussion).
primary not_stated: no outcome is named primary and no preregistration is mentioned. The rubric answers RQ4 on painting skills (p. 2, RQ4; p. 6, Data analysis).

Criterion 3 holds: S1-O1 is the teachers' 'Creativity and Originality' rating of each student's painting, treatment 4.581 (SD 0.444) against control 4.205 (SD 0.499), t = 3.515 (p. 6, Stage 4; p. 11, Table 9).
summary: Criterion 3 holds: three teachers scored every student's Task 2 painting on a 1 to 5 rubric, and for all five rubric outcomes the form's numbers, measure (expert_raters), unit (participant, n = 39 per arm), and direction match Table 9 and the Methods. The coding is still refuted on details: the paper never says the AI-generated images were available while students painted, so 'ai_available_when_produced: yes' and with_ai rest on inference, and the usefulness code for Technical Skill and Composition and Design is not supported by the item text and conflicts with the c059 handling of proficiency ratings.
